Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association (MMA)
In Support of
LD 1044, An Act to Clarijj� the Qualifling Use of Tax Increment Financing
for Extension of a Development District
April 2, 2025
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Taxation, my name is Amanda Campbell, and I am submitting testimony in support of LD 1044 on
behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC).
Current law allows for a twenty-year extension to a TIF district if the extension begins after the general effective date of the law enacted during the First Special Session of the 1315` Legislature and if that
district uses at least 75% of its TIF revenue on either affordable housing or transit-oriented projects.
LD 1044 would clarify that the ten-year period begins on October 25, 2023 and would allow the usage of
TIF district revenues, totaling the currently allowed 75%, for either affordable housing or transit related projects or both. The bill also updates the definition of transit-oriented development.
Municipal officials support these proposed updates to TIF law as they provide additional tools to facilitate economic development for communities that wish to use them.
Thank you for your consideration of the municipal perspective. Please feel free to contact any member of
the LPC or the MMA Advocacy team with any questions relating to municipal operations.

Testimony ofRepresentative Amy D. Kuhn introducing
LD 1044, An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing
for Extension of a Development District
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier and distinguished members of the Taxation
Committee, my name is Amy Kuhn, and I proudly represent House District 111 in the town of Falmouth. It is a pleasure to be with you today to introduce LD 1044, An Act to Clarify the
Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District.
This bill offers two discrete clarifications to a bill passed in the 131" Legislature. LD 1739
allowed a tax increment financing (TIF) district to be extended an additional 20 years at the
original valuation if the district uses at least 75% of TIF revenue for any combination of affordable housing or transit-oriented development. Upon implementation of the law, however,
certain vagueness in the statutory language was discovered.
To correct those ambiguities, this bill clarifies two important components of the previously
enacted law. First, it clarifies that transit-oriented development under this extension need not be located in the development district. This was an important part of last year's bill because it allowed development outside the TIF district that could then be connected to a growth area by transit. Second, the bill clarifies that the TIF revenue can be spent on any combination of affordable housing and/or transit, as opposed to one or the other.
On this second point, I have received the proposed language from the Department of Economic
Community Development, which they believe better addresses the issue than the language proposed in the bill I submitted. The suggestion for line 10 is as follows:
. . " .extended an additional 20 years if the district uses in total at least 75% of tax increment
Q _
financing revenue for affordable housing projects and/or transit-oriented development, both..."
I appreciate the Department's input and am happy to adopt their suggestion.
It is important to recognize that both components were fully debated and adopted in the 131"
Legislature's consideration of LD 1739. For example, my introductory testimony on LD 1739
District 111: Falmouth (part)

includes the statement, "[t]he bill under discussion today. . .w0uld allow for an extension of an additional 30 years at the original valuation so long as a majority of the funds are put towards
affordable housing and/or transit-related projects," dated May 10, 2023.
Finally, I should note that the law, as enacted, included a ten-year sunset provision. The committee arrived at this compromise to give municipalities additional tools to address Maine's urgent needs in relation to affordable housing and climate goals while not over-privileging any community benefiting from TIFs. At the end of the ten-year period, the typical TIF district
duration will resume.
To summarize, the language amendments sought here simply align the implementation of this
law with the Legislature's intent. Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to present this bill
to the committee.

Testimony in Support of LD 1044
An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District
April 2, 2025

Senator Grolioski, Representative Cloutier and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Taxation, my name is Jay Brenchick, and I am submitting testimony in strong support of LD 1044 Act to
Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District. This legislation represents an essential step in strengthening Maine's ability to support and sustain affordable housing and transit-oriented development through the strategic use of tax increment financing (TIF).

The proposed changes clarity and ensure that municipalities can effectively utilize TIF revenue for these critical investments, which are fundamental to fostering economic growth, community resilience, and equitable access
to housing and transportation.

Key Benefits of This Legislation:
1. Enhancing Affordable Housing Access: The housing crisis remains a significant challenge across Maine. Allowing extended use of TIF revenues to develop safe, quality housing for households earning up to 120% of the area median income ensures that more Mainers can find stable and affordable living
situations.
2. Supporting Transit-Oriented Development: By refining the definition of transit-oriented development
to include areas beyond designated districts or nodes, this bill recognizes that transportation infrastructure can serve a broader range of communities and economic development opportunities.
3. Providing Long-Term Economic Stability: The ability to extend TIF districts ensures that municipalities can plan and execute long-term investments in housing and transit that align with Maine's
economic and environmental sustainability goals. 4. Strengthening Workforce and Economic Growth: Ensuring that workers have access to affordable
housing and reliable transportation options supports local businesses, attracts new talent, and creates a
more vibrant and economically inclusive state.
As Maine continues to address the interconnected challenges of housing affordability and infrastructure development, this legislation provides a crucial tool for municipalities to build stronger, more sustainable
communities

Testimony in Support of LD 1044:
An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for

April 2, 2025
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier and esteemed members of the Committee on
Taxation, my name is Maureen Terry, legislative liaison for the Department of
Community and Economic Development (DECD), and I am here today to testify in
strong support of LD 1044, "An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment
Financing for Extension of a Development District."
Tax Increment Financing (TIF) is a crucial tool for municipalities to drive economic growth, enhance housing opportunities, and invest in community infrastructure. This bill provides clarity for a change made to the program in the 131" legislature, creating criteria for extending a TIF district, ensuring that municipalities can confidently utilize TIF funds
to support affordable housing and transit-oriented development. By explicitly stating that
tax increment financing revenue can be allocated to one or both of these essential uses, this legislation offers flexibility for local governments to meet the unique needs of their communities.
DECD supports this clarifying language to ensure clear and unambiguous application
moving forward.
This legislation aligns with Maine's broader goals of fostering smart growth, ensuring
equitable housing opportunities, and promoting environmentally conscious infrastructure. It also provides municipalities with the certainty they need to proceed with long-term planning efforts, knowing that their TIF investments will be honored under state law.
For these reasons, I strongly urge this committee to support LD 1044 and vote it forward
for enactment. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I am happy to answer any questions you may have.

Testimony of Mayor of the City of Portland, Mark Dion
Before Committee on Taxation
In Support of
LD 1044 - An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for the Extension of a Development District
April 2, 2025  Dear Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and Members of the Committee,
On behalf of the City of Portland, I write in support of LD 1044, An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for the Extension of a Development District.
Portland has long used Tax Increment Financing (TIF) as a flexible, locally controlled tool to support affordable housing, transit-oriented development, and community infrastructure. These investments are essential to ensuring our city can grow in a way that is equitable, sustainable, and responsive to the needs of all residents.
LD 1044 makes a modest but important clarification to existing law: that the use of TIF revenues to support affordable housing and transit-oriented development qualifies a municipality for a 20-year extension of the TIF district, consistent with the policy intent of the original statute. This clarity is particularly important as municipalities like Portland seek to assemble long-term financing plans that align with local comprehensive plans, state housing goals, and climate commitments.
As Maine's largest and most densely populated city, Portland faces unique challenges in developing and preserving housing that is affordable to working families. TIF revenues have been a critical part of how we fund affordable housing projects in neighborhoods that are otherwise experiencing displacement and gentrification pressures. Likewise, we have used TIF to invest in infrastructure that supports smart growth, walkability, and public transit--tools that help reduce carbon emissions and build more connected communities.

By affirming that these uses are not only allowable but also qualify a district for the full extension available under law, LD 1044 provides municipalities with the predictability and certainty they need to plan for the long term. It also ensures that the state's TIF statute remains aligned with evolving community needs and policy goals. We are grateful to Representative Kuhn for sponsoring this bill, and to the Legislature for continuing to recognize the value of municipal tools that promote both economic development and housing equity. For these reasons, I respectfully urge the Committee to vote Ought to Pass on LD 1044. Thank you for your time and consideration.

TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: Wednesday, April 2, 2025
LD 1044 - "An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District"
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee - good afternoon, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Neither For Nor Against LD 1044, "An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District."
From a technical perspective, it is unclear how it would be determined that jobs, and retail or service establishments "rely" on transit as one of the "means of meeting transportation needs." This should be clarified.
Shifting to the Administration's legal and statutory concerns, the bill's amended definition of "transit-oriented development" creates a disparity between the existing definition of the same term under 30-A M.R.S. � 5222. In addition, the bill broadens eligibility for municipalities to exceed the 30-year cap for TIF districts, but does not expand eligibility for the parallel affordable housing TIF statute under 30-A M.R.S. � 5248. It is unclear whether this was the intent of the bill.
Any fiscal and administrative costs associated with the bill can be absorbed under current budgetary allotments.
1

In summation, the Administration is Neither For Nor Against L.D. 1044 because we concerns about the expansion in eligibility and uses of TIFs in recent years. We suggest that the committee review this bill in coordination with DECD.
The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.

Re: Support for LD 1044; An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District
Senate Chair Nicole Grohoski, House Chair Kristen Cloutier and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation:
I, Nathan Poore, Town Manager of the Town of Falmouth testify in support of LD 1044.
I am writing to express my strong support for the proposed bill that clarifies the language in the Tax Increment Financing (TIF) district regulations, which provide an extension of up to 20 years for districts that allocate at least 75% of their TIF revenue to affordable housing projects or transit-oriented development, or both. This important distinction will allow municipalities to maximize TIF revenues for both affordable housing and transit needs in the community. This change to the statute is a crucial step toward addressing the pressing needs of our communities in Maine, and I believe it will significantly contribute to the state's growth and sustainability.
Furthermore, the ability to use TIF revenues for Transit Oriented Development outside the TIF district is key for connecting housing to growth areas as well as other economic hubs in Town. This change will create more livable cities and towns, hence driving an increase in economic development.
I strongly urge the committee to support this bill, which provides Maine municipalities with the tools and flexibility they need to address the affordable housing crisis and promote sustainable, transit-friendly development.
